newsitem.title: USA: Simpson lawyer joins team defending British nanny.
newsitem.headline: Simpson lawyer joins team defending British nanny.

text.p: One of the members of O.J. Simpson's defence team was officially admitted on Wednesday to the team of the lawyers defending a British nanny accused of killing a 9-month-old baby.
Barry Scheck, who was part of the team that won an acquittal for the former pro-football player accused of murdering his ex-wife and her friend, was formally admitted to the Middlesex Superior Court.
He will be handling any testimony in the complex legal field known as DNA testing for the defence of Louise Woodward, a 19-year-old from Chester, England, who is accused of killing Matthew Eappen.

The baby died as a result of severe head injuries. Police testified that Woodward, who came to the United States last summer to work as an au pair, violently shook the infant and dropped him on the bathroom floor.

But defence lawyer Andrew Good persuaded Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel to allow the dead infant's tissue to be DNA tested to see if the baby suffered from a genetic defect that made him prone to skull injuries.

Good, in papers filed earlier this week, also said he intended to call on a number medical experts, including famed pathologist Michael Baden, the former New York City coroner, who will testify that the injuries could have been sustained anywhere from 12 hours to two days before the baby was rushed to a local hospital on Feb. 4.
Judge Zobel set a firm date of Oct. 6 for Woodward's trial. She has been held without bail since her arrest in early February.
